followUps: Return token objects with start/end offsets.
Add quoted strings and escape sequences.
Support streaming input where a token can span chunks.
followUpGuide: For offsets, append small records like `{token, start, end}` with each emitted token. Keep the trie walk unchanged.
For quoted strings, branch before trie lookup when the current character is a quote. Use an explicit state machine so escape handling stays local.
For streaming, keep a suffix buffer for characters that might form a longer token in the next chunk. Clarify maximum token length so the buffer remains bounded.
complexityAnalysis: - Naive prefix scan: try every vocabulary token at each position. Time: O(L * V * T), where L is input length, V vocab size, T token length. Space: O(1) besides output.

- Trie approach: build the trie from S total vocabulary characters, then walk candidates and keep the last terminal match. Time: O(S + L * max(1, m)), where m is max token length. Empty vocab still requires scanning whitespace or finding the first unknown character. Space: O(S) besides output.

- DP follow-up: define an objective for valid or globally optimal segmentation as a separate contract. With trie transitions, time: O(S + L * m). Space: O(S + L) besides output. The required greedy problem fails at its first unmatched position and never backtracks.
solutionGuide: A trie gives clean longest-prefix lookup without scanning every vocabulary item at each position.
Track the last terminal node seen while walking forward. If the walk stops, emit that last terminal token and advance to its end.
raise ValueError("vocab cannot contain empty tokens")
